cd ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/gatorwalk-factory/references/examples && cat build-swamp-extension.yaml
cat ${HOME}/.claude/projects/-HOME--cue-work-gatorwalk-test-drive-scratch-repo2/3dc34d08-ebe6-484f-8034-e29c8785dcef/tool-results/bdk3vov6y.txt

swamp model create @swamp/gatorwalk-factory/tracker board --global-arg prefix=oas --json && swamp model create @swamp/gatorwalk-factory/factory openapi --global-arg tracker=board --json && cat models/@swamp/gatorwalk-factory/factory/openapi.yaml

cd ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/gatorwalk-factory/references && grep -n -B2 -A4 "maxCycles" *.md examples/*.yaml | head -60; grep -n "^#" driving.md

cat > models/@swamp/gatorwalk-factory/factory/openapi.yaml <<'EOF'
type: '@swamp/gatorwalk-factory/factory'
typeVersion: 2026.09.30.1
id: eac2dea5-1d63-462f-aede-925d614e35ca
name: openapi
version: 1
tags: {}
globalArguments:
  tracker: board
  definition:
    schemaVersion: 1
    description: |-
      Turn an OpenAPI spec into a swamp extension: one model type per API
      resource, one method per operation, zod schemas from the spec's
      component schemas, and auth from its securitySchemes with secrets read
      from a vault. Each work item carries one spec (a path or URL).

      The plan is the breakdown: which resources become which model types,
      which operations become which methods, what is left out and why. Before
      planning, the existing extensions are searched (swamp extension search),
      so an API that already has an extension is not built again.

      People decide at three points: approving the breakdown, approving the
      landing, and abandoning the work. A person can also always send the work
      back by hand (revise, recheck), so declining an approval never leaves
      abandon as the only way out.

      Done means the generated extension passes swamp extension fmt, the type
      check and a smoke test (one model per type, one read-only method, against
      the live API or a mock when there are no credentials), and the reviewed
      commit is on the repository's default branch. It lands by direct commit;
      nothing is pushed to a registry. Every check and the landing are bound to
      the commit named in change-summary, the commit that was reviewed.

    stages:
      - id: plan
        initial: true
        tracker:
          status: open
          entries:
            - on: { record: plan }
              cycle: first
              step: plan_generated
              emoji: "📝"
              summary: "Breakdown generated (v{{$version}}): {{summary}}"
            - on: { record: plan }
              cycle: later
              step: plan_revised
              emoji: "🔄"
              summary: "Breakdown revised (v{{$version}}), round {{$cycle}}: {{summary}}"
          duplicate:
            on: { approve: duplicate-confirmation }
            record: duplicate-of
            field: primary
        description: >-
          Read the OpenAPI spec and plan how it breaks down into swamp model
          types and methods, after checking no existing extension covers it.
        work:
          mode: interactive
          systemPrompt: |
            First, check the work is not a duplicate of another ticket. If it
            is, find out whether that ticket, the primary, already has a work
            item: run the tracker's claim on it with dryRun=true, which writes
            nothing. Record duplicate-of with the primary's stable id, its
            display id and why, and wait for a person to approve
            duplicate-confirmation; do not plan. Once it is approved, move the
            work to the primary. When the primary has no work item, retarget
            this work item onto the primary's externalRefs and publish at once,
            then plan the primary's work here. When it has one, take the
            duplicate exit.

            Fetch the OpenAPI spec named on the ticket and read it whole. Then
            search before building: run swamp extension search and
            swamp model type search for the API, and record what you searched
            and found under reuse. If an extension already covers the API, say
            so in the plan and recommend extending or using it instead.

            Plan the breakdown. Group operations into resources by tag, or by
            path prefix when the spec has no tags; each resource becomes one
            model type named @<collective>/<api>/<resource>. Each operation
            becomes one method, named for what it does (list, get, create,
            update, delete, or a verb for an action), with its HTTP method and
            path. List every operation you leave out, with why (deprecated,
            needs a scope we will not have, duplicated by another). Say how auth
            works (the securityScheme, the header, and the vault secret that
            holds the key) and how the smoke test will run: against the live
            API when a key is available, otherwise against a mock.

            On a later plan, read the injected plan (the last one),
            plan-review (its review) and plan-feedback (the person's latest
            feedback); the first plan has none of them. After rework, address
            the review's open critical and high findings. After revise, address
            the feedback. Record feedbackIncorporated as the last plan's list,
            adding the feedback word for word unless it is already the list's
            last entry.
          context:
            inject: [plan, plan-review, plan-feedback]
        artifacts:
          - name: plan
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [summary, spec, reuse, extension, models, auth, testingStrategy]
              properties:
                summary: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                spec:
                  type: object
                  required: [source, title, version, openapiVersion, operationCount]
                  additionalProperties: false
                  properties:
                    source: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    title: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    version: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    openapiVersion: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    operationCount: { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
                reuse:
                  type: object
                  required: [searched, decision, reason]
                  additionalProperties: false
                  properties:
                    searched:
                      type: array
                      minItems: 1
                      items: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    found:
                      type: array
                      items: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    decision: { enum: [build-new, extend-existing, use-existing] }
                    reason: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                extension:
                  type: object
                  required: [name, directory]
                  additionalProperties: false
                  properties:
                    name: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    directory: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                models:
                  type: array
                  minItems: 1
                  items:
                    type: object
                    required: [type, resource, methods]
                    additionalProperties: false
                    properties:
                      type: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                      resource: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                      description: { type: string }
                      methods:
                        type: array
                        minItems: 1
                        items:
                          type: object
                          required: [name, httpMethod, path]
                          additionalProperties: false
                          properties:
                            name: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                            httpMethod:
                              enum: [GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS]
                            path: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                            operationId: { type: string }
                            readOnly: { type: boolean }
                excluded:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: object
                    required: [operation, reason]
                    additionalProperties: false
                    properties:
                      operation: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                      reason: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                auth:
                  type: object
                  required: [scheme, vaultSecret]
                  additionalProperties: false
                  properties:
                    scheme: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                    header: { type: string }
                    vaultSecret: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                testingStrategy: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                feedbackIncorporated:
                  description: >-
                    Every round of a person's plan feedback this plan answers,
                    oldest first.
                  type: array
                  items: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
          - name: duplicate-of
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [primary, display, reason]
              additionalProperties: false
              properties:
                primary:
                  description: The primary ticket's stable id.
                  type: string
                  minLength: 1
                display:
                  description: The primary ticket's display id.
                  type: string
                  minLength: 1
                reason: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
        transitions:
          - name: submit
            to: plan-review
            gates:
              - type: artifact-exists
                config: { artifact: plan }
          - name: duplicate
            to: duplicate
            description: >-
              The work duplicates a primary ticket that already has a work item;
              a person confirms it. When the primary has none, the work item is
              retargeted onto it instead, and the cel gate closes this exit to
              it.
            gates:
              - type: human-approval
                config: { id: duplicate-confirmation }
              - type: cel
                config:
                  expr: >-
                    "duplicate-of" in artifacts &&
                    (!("builtin" in item.externalRefs) ||
                    item.externalRefs["builtin"] !=
                    artifacts["duplicate-of"].payload.primary)
                  message: >-
                    this work item is on the primary ticket now; plan it here

      - id: plan-review
        tracker:
          status: open
          entries:
            - on: { record: plan-review }
              step: plan_reviewed
              emoji: "🔍"
              summary: >-
                Breakdown review (plan v{{$version.plan}}): {{count findings
                severity=critical}} critical, {{count findings severity=high}}
                high, {{count findings}} in all
            - on: { approve: plan-approval }
              step: plan_approved
              emoji: "✅"
              summary: "Breakdown approved (v{{$version.plan}})"
        description: >-
          Adversarial review of the breakdown against the spec. Approval needs a
          fresh review with no open critical or high findings and a person's
          sign-off; open critical or high findings send the plan back. revise is
          for when the person wants the breakdown itself changed.
        work:
          mode: dispatch
          systemPrompt: |
            You are an adversarial reviewer of a plan that breaks the OpenAPI
            spec at {{specSource}} into swamp model types:
            {{planSummary}}
            Fetch the spec and check the plan against it: every operation is
            either a method or listed under excluded with a reason; resources
            are grouped sensibly (a model type a person would recognise, not one
            per path and not one for the whole API); method names say what they
            do; auth matches the spec's securitySchemes and keeps the key in a
            vault; and the reuse search was real, so an existing extension is
            not rebuilt.
            Rate a finding critical or high only if the plan would ship a
            defect, leave an operation silently missing, put a secret outside a
            vault, rebuild an extension that already exists, or make the smoke
            test meaningless. Naming taste, grouping preferences and process
            gaps are medium at most. Judge the plan against the size of the
            spec, and give the smallest adequate fix for each finding. Report
            findings with severities, and do not soften the severity of a real
            defect.
          bindings:
            planSummary: artifacts["plan"].payload.summary
            specSource: artifacts["plan"].payload.spec.source
          context:
            inject: [plan]
        artifacts:
          - name: plan-review
            kind: findings
            reviews: plan
        evidence:
          - name: plan-feedback
            description: >-
              A person's feedback on the breakdown, in their words; revise needs
              it.
            recordedBy: person
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [feedback]
              additionalProperties: false
              properties:
                feedback: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
        transitions:
          - name: approve
            to: implement
            gates:
              - type: artifact-fresh
                config: { artifact: plan-review, recordedThisCycle: true }
              - type: findings-clear
                config: { artifact: plan-review, blocking: [critical, high] }
              - type: human-approval
                config: { id: plan-approval }
          - name: rework
            to: plan
            description: >-
              The fresh breakdown review has an open critical or high finding,
              so the plan goes back to be fixed.
            gates:
              - type: artifact-fresh
                config: { artifact: plan-review, recordedThisCycle: true }
              - type: cel
                config:
                  expr: >-
                    "plan-review" in artifacts &&
                    artifacts["plan-review"].payload.findings.exists(f,
                    (f.severity == "critical" || f.severity == "high") &&
                    !(has(f.resolved) && f.resolved))
                  message: rework needs an open critical or high finding
          - name: revise
            to: plan
            manual: true
            description: >-
              A person declined the breakdown without a blocking finding, to
              change it and have it reviewed again. Manual, and the person's
              feedback is recorded first, so every revision carries its reason.
            gates:
              - type: evidence-recorded
                description: The person's feedback on this plan is recorded.
                config: { name: plan-feedback }

      - id: implement
        maxCycles: 4
        tracker: { status: in_progress }
        description: >-
          Generate the extension from the approved breakdown and commit it.
          Bounded at four entries: the first build and three rounds back from a
          failed check or a blocking review.
        work:
          mode: interactive
          systemPrompt: |
            Build the extension in the plan's directory, one model type per
            planned model and one method per planned method. Derive zod schemas
            from the spec's component schemas, read the API key from the vault
            secret the plan names, and pin explicit versions on any npm: import.
            Use the swamp skill for extension structure.
            Commit the work, then record change-summary with the full SHA of the
            commit you want checked and reviewed. After rework, record it again
            for the new commit.
          context:
            inject: [plan, plan-review]
        artifacts:
          - name: change-summary
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [summary, commit, files, modelTypes]
              properties:
                summary: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                commit: { type: string, pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{40}$" }
                files: { type: array, minItems: 1, items: { type: string } }
                modelTypes:
                  type: array
                  minItems: 1
                  items: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
        transitions:
          - name: submit
            to: check
            gates:
              - type: artifact-exists
                config: { artifact: change-summary }
              - type: cel
                config:
                  expr: >-
                    !("checks" in evidence) ||
                    evidence["checks"].payload.commit !=
                    artifacts["change-summary"].payload.commit
                  message: >-
                    change-summary still names the commit already checked;
                    record it for the new commit
          - name: recheck
            to: check
            manual: true
            description: >-
              Check the same commit again, for a failure that was not the code's
              (a flaky API, a broken tool). A person decides.

      - id: check
        tracker:
          status: in_progress
          entries:
            - on: dispatch
              step: checks_started
              emoji: "🧪"
              summary: "Checks started on {{$input.commit}}, attempt {{$cycle}}"
            - on: { record: checks }
              match: { status: passed }
              step: checks_passed
              emoji: "✅"
              summary: "Checks passed on {{commit}}"
            - on: { record: checks }
              match: { status: failed }
              step: checks_failed
              emoji: "❌"
              summary: "Checks failed on {{commit}}"
        description: >-
          Run swamp extension fmt, the type check and a smoke test on the
          change-summary commit. The smoke test creates one model of each
          generated type and runs one read-only method, against the live API
          when a key is in the vault and a mock otherwise.
        work:
          mode: interactive
          systemPrompt: |
            Check commit {{commit}}. Run swamp extension fmt (check only), the
            type check, then the smoke test: create one model of each generated
            type and run one read-only method on each, against the live API if
            the vault holds a key, otherwise against a mock of the spec. Record
            checks with one result per step and say which target the smoke test
            used. Delete the smoke-test models afterwards.
          bindings:
            commit: artifacts["change-summary"].payload.commit
        evidence:
          - name: checks
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [commit, status, smokeTarget, results]
              properties:
                commit: { type: string, pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{40}$" }
                status: { enum: [passed, failed] }
                smokeTarget: { enum: [live, mock] }
                results:
                  type: array
                  minItems: 1
                  items:
                    type: object
                    required: [name, status]
                    additionalProperties: false
                    properties:
                      name: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                      status: { enum: [passed, failed, skipped] }
                      detail: { type: string }
              $comment: An overall pass cannot contain a failed result.
              if:
                properties: { status: { const: passed } }
              then:
                properties:
                  results:
                    not:
                      contains:
                        properties: { status: { const: failed } }
        transitions:
          - name: passed
            to: code-review
            gates:
              - type: evidence-recorded
                config: { name: checks, requireField: { status: passed } }
              - type: cel
                config:
                  expr: >-
                    evidence["checks"].payload.commit ==
                    artifacts["change-summary"].payload.commit
                  message: checks must be for the change-summary commit
          - name: failed
            to: implement
            description: >-
              The checks failed, so the extension goes back to be fixed.
            gates:
              - type: evidence-recorded
                config: { name: checks, requireField: { status: failed } }

      - id: code-review
        tracker:
          status: in_progress
          entries:
            - on: { record: code-review }
              step: code_reviewed
              emoji: "🔍"
              summary: >-
                Code review (change v{{$version.change-summary}}): {{count
                findings severity=critical}} critical, {{count findings
                severity=high}} high, {{count findings}} in all
            - on: { approve: land-approval }
              step: land_approved
              emoji: "✅"
              summary: "Landing approved (change v{{$version.change-summary}})"
        description: >-
          Adversarial review of the checked extension against the approved
          breakdown. Landing needs a fresh review with no open critical or high
          findings and a person's approval; open critical or high findings send
          the change back.
        work:
          mode: dispatch
          systemPrompt: |
            You are an adversarial reviewer. Review commit {{commit}}:
            {{changeSummary}}
            Check it against the approved breakdown: every planned method exists
            and calls the planned HTTP method and path, request and response
            schemas match the spec, the API key comes only from the vault, and
            npm: imports pin explicit versions.
            Rate a finding critical or high only if the change would ship a
            defect (a wrong path, a wrong schema, a missing planned method),
            leak a secret, or make the smoke test meaningless. Style and naming
            are low; process gaps the checks already cover are medium at most.
            Judge the change against its size, and give the smallest adequate
            fix for each finding. Report findings with severities, and do not
            soften the severity of a real defect.
          bindings:
            commit: artifacts["change-summary"].payload.commit
            changeSummary: artifacts["change-summary"].payload.summary
          context:
            inject: [plan, change-summary, checks]
        artifacts:
          - name: code-review
            kind: findings
            reviews: change-summary
        transitions:
          - name: accept
            to: land
            gates:
              - type: artifact-fresh
                config: { artifact: code-review, recordedThisCycle: true }
              - type: findings-clear
                config: { artifact: code-review, blocking: [critical, high] }
              - type: human-approval
                config: { id: land-approval }
          - name: rework
            to: implement
            description: >-
              The fresh code review has an open critical or high finding, so the
              change goes back to be fixed.
            gates:
              - type: artifact-fresh
                config: { artifact: code-review, recordedThisCycle: true }
              - type: cel
                config:
                  expr: >-
                    "code-review" in artifacts &&
                    artifacts["code-review"].payload.findings.exists(f,
                    (f.severity == "critical" || f.severity == "high") &&
                    !(has(f.resolved) && f.resolved))
                  message: rework needs an open critical or high finding
          - name: revise
            to: implement
            manual: true
            description: >-
              A person declined the landing without a blocking finding; change
              the work. Manual, so it never fires on its own.

      - id: land
        tracker:
          status: in_progress
          entries:
            - on: { transition: landed }
              step: complete
              emoji: "🏁"
              summary: "Landed {{$input.commit}}"
        description: >-
          Land the reviewed commit by direct commit: make sure it is on the
          repository's default branch, and record the branch it landed on.
        work:
          mode: interactive
          systemPrompt: |
            Land commit {{commit}} on the default branch with a direct commit
            (fast-forward or it is already there; never rewrite it). Record
            landed with the commit and the branch, after confirming with
            git branch --contains that the branch holds it.
          bindings:
            commit: artifacts["change-summary"].payload.commit
        evidence:
          - name: landed
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [via, commit, branch]
              additionalProperties: false
              properties:
                via: { enum: [direct-commit] }
                commit: { type: string, pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{40}$" }
                branch: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
        transitions:
          - name: landed
            to: done
            gates:
              - type: evidence-recorded
                config: { name: landed }
              - type: cel
                config:
                  expr: >-
                    evidence["landed"].payload.commit ==
                    artifacts["change-summary"].payload.commit
                  message: the landing must be the reviewed commit
          - name: rework
            to: implement
            manual: true
            description: The landing was blocked; go back and change the work.

      - id: done
        terminal: true
        tracker: { status: shipped }

      - id: duplicate
        terminal: true
        description: >-
          The work duplicated a primary ticket that has its own work item.
        tracker: { status: closed }

      - id: abandoned
        terminal: true
        tracker: { status: closed }

    globalTransitions:
      - name: abandon
        to: abandoned
        gates:
          - type: human-approval
            config: { id: abandon-confirmation }

  scenarios:
    - scenario: plan-waits-for-approval
      description: >-
        A breakdown with a clean review still waits for a person's approval
        before any code is generated.
      steps:
        - record: { artifact: plan }
          payload: &plan
            summary: Petstore as two model types
            spec: { source: petstore.yaml, title: Petstore, version: "1", openapiVersion: "3.0.0", operationCount: 2 }
            reuse: { searched: [petstore], decision: build-new, reason: nothing found }
            extension: { name: "@me/petstore", directory: extensions/models/petstore }
            models:
              - type: "@me/petstore/pet"
                resource: pet
                methods: [{ name: list, httpMethod: GET, path: /pets, readOnly: true }]
              - type: "@me/petstore/store"
                resource: store
                methods: [{ name: inventory, httpMethod: GET, path: /store/inventory, readOnly: true }]
            auth: { scheme: apiKey, header: api_key, vaultSecret: petstore/api-key }
            testingStrategy: Smoke test list against a mock
        - move: submit
        - record: { artifact: plan-review }
          payload: { findings: [] }
        - move: approve
          expect: { refused: plan-approval }
        - wait: 1800
          note: The person reads the breakdown and the review
        - approve: plan-approval
        - move: approve
        - expect: { stage: implement }

    - scenario: blocking-review-reworks-plan
      description: >-
        A high finding on the breakdown (an operation silently missing) sends
        the plan back on its own.
      steps:
        - record: { artifact: plan }
          payload: *plan
        - move: submit
        - record: { artifact: plan-review }
          payload: { findings: [{ id: F1, severity: high, description: DELETE /pets/{id} is neither planned nor excluded }] }
        - move: approve
          expect: { refused: "" }
        - move: rework
        - expect: { stage: plan }

    - scenario: failed-check-bounded
      description: >-
        A failed check always goes back to implement, at most three times; the
        fourth failure is refused until a person grants one more pass.
      steps:
        - record: { artifact: plan }
          payload: *plan
        - move: submit
        - record: { artifact: plan-review }
          payload: { findings: [] }
        - approve: plan-approval
        - move: approve
        - record: { artifact: change-summary }
          payload: { summary: s, commit: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111, files: [a.ts], modelTypes: ["@me/petstore/pet"] }
        - move: submit
        - record: { evidence: checks }
          payload: { commit: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111, status: failed, smokeTarget: mock, results: [{ name: typecheck, status: failed }] }
        - move: failed
        - record: { artifact: change-summary }
          payload: { summary: s, commit: 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, files: [a.ts], modelTypes: ["@me/petstore/pet"] }
        - move: submit
        - record: { evidence: checks }
          payload: { commit: 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, status: failed, smokeTarget: mock, results: [{ name: typecheck, status: failed }] }
        - move: failed
        - record: { artifact: change-summary }
          payload: { summary: s, commit: 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333, files: [a.ts], modelTypes: ["@me/petstore/pet"] }
        - move: submit
        - record: { evidence: checks }
          payload: { commit: 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333, status: failed, smokeTarget: mock, results: [{ name: typecheck, status: failed }] }
        - move: failed
        - record: { artifact: change-summary }
          payload: { summary: s, commit: 4444444444444444444444444444444444444444, files: [a.ts], modelTypes: ["@me/petstore/pet"] }
        - move: submit
        - record: { evidence: checks }
          payload: { commit: 4444444444444444444444444444444444444444, status: failed, smokeTarget: mock, results: [{ name: typecheck, status: failed }] }
        - move: failed
          expect: { refused: "cycle override for 'implement'" }
        - override: { stage: implement, note: one more pass }
        - move: failed
        - expect: { stage: implement }

    - scenario: spec-to-landed
      description: >-
        A spec walks the whole way: the breakdown is reviewed and approved, the
        extension is checked against a mock, reviewed, approved and landed by
        direct commit.
      steps:
        - record: { artifact: plan }
          payload: *plan
        - move: submit
        - record: { artifact: plan-review }
          payload: { findings: [{ id: F1, severity: low, description: Naming }] }
        - approve: plan-approval
